subject.title: fix(sessions): keep dirty transcript search from blocking the gateway

question: Does OpenClaw want to adopt this persisted claim-token and single-worker reconciliation protocol as the canonical dirty transcript-index lifecycle?
rationale: The patch appears functionally sound and now has real behavior proof, but automation cannot decide whether overloading the persisted dirty flag, the timeout hierarchy, and process-wide serialization are the desired long-term session-state contract.

options.title: Adopt after owner review
options.body: Rebase onto current main, audit all dirty-state readers and timeout ordering, then merge the worker-and-claim design if exact-head proof remains green.

options.title: Request a narrower protocol
options.body: Keep worker isolation but ask for a dedicated persisted claim field or simpler ownership lifecycle before merging.

options.title: Pause the redesign
options.body: Leave the issue open and close this PR if maintainers do not want a new persisted reconciliation protocol for transcript search.

recommendation.title: Adopt after owner review
recommendation.body: Rebase onto current main, audit all dirty-state readers and timeout ordering, then merge the worker-and-claim design if exact-head proof remains green.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available current-main history signal is the recent transcript architecture refactor attributed to steipete.
